3. At the out set, memo came to be filed.
Placing the memo on record petition against petitioner No.3 is dismissed as he has been arrested and the petition has become infructuous.

4. The brief facts of the case are as under:
A complaint came to be lodged by Smt. Madhuri W/o Guruprasad for the offences punishable under Sections 498A of Indian Penal Code (for short 'IPC) R/w Sectio 34 of IPC and Section 4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act, 1961 and registered in Crime No.
17/2023 on 26.01.2023 by Varthur Police Station.
5.

The gist of the complaint averments reveal that the complainant was married to Sri. Guruprasad and thereafter they led a married life for sometime in a happy manner and a son aged about 6 years was born in the marriage.
The complainant further stated that her husband had illicit relationship with others and in that regard they demanded dowry from the parents of the complainant and he was harassing the complainant.
6. Later on, the father of the complainant lodged another complaint stating that complaint in Cr.No.17/2023 was done to death in a suspicious manner.
A case came to be registered based on the said complaint under Section 304B IPC.
The matter is being investigated.

Husband of the Madhuri was arrested and during the pendency of the present petition, brother-in-law of the deceased Sri.
Pramod is also arrested.
Thus the remaining petitioners are the parents-in-law of deceased Smt.Madhuri.
7. The attempt made by the petitioners to obtain grant of anticipatory bail is turned-down by learned District Judge vide order dated 10.03.2023 in Criminal Misc. No. 368/2023.
Thereafter, the petitioners are before this Court.

8. Sri. M.S. Shyam Sunder, learned Senior counsel for the petitioners reiterating the grounds urged in the bail petition vehemently contended that petitioners are the father-in-law and mother-in-law of the deceased and aged 73 years and 67 years respectively had no role or whatsoever in the alleged incident and they are innocent of the offences alleged against them and they are ready to cooperate with the investigation agency and therefore, they may be granted anticipatory bail.

9. Per contra, Sri. Vinayaka V.S., learned High Court Government Pleader vehemently contended non appearance of the present petitioners has resulted in scuttling the investigation process backward and sought for rejection of bail petition.
10.

Sri. Shankar Narayana Rao, learned Senior counsel representing the defacto complainant who is the father of the deceased, vehemently contended that material on record would goes to show that the husband of Smt. Madhuri, who is non other than the son of the petitioners No.1 and 2 had illicit Mr. K. Raghavendra Rao vs State Of Karnataka By Varthur P S on 20 April, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/136257447/
3 relationship and had publically claimed that the marriage with the Smt. Madhuri is only for the purpose of society and he being the male, can have any number of relationship out side the marriage and in order to have his ambitions cleared, all petitioners including husband of the Smt. Madhuri have conspired to the death and ended life of Smt. Madhuri, said offence being a heinous in nature and a menace in the society, the petitioners are not entitled for bail.

sentences.text: 11. In view of the rival contentions, this Court perused the materials on record meticulously.
12. On such perusal of the material on record, it is seen that Smt. Madhuri in her life time also lodged complaint and thereafter, father of the Madhuri has lodged complaint.

Smt.Madhuri in her complaint has stated that the accused No.1 being the son of the petitioners No.1 and 2 had illicit relationship and in that regard, he was demanding dowry and was harassing the Smt. Madhuri.
13. Subsequently, when Smt. Madhuri died, a case came to be registered based on the complaint given by father of the Smt. Madhuri under Section 304B and provisions of Dowry Provision Act.
From the date of registration of the case, the present petitioners are not available to the investigation agency.
The attempt made by them having been failed, they have approached this court for grant of anticipatory bail.
14. Fact remains that non appearance of the present petitioners before the investigation agency has also resulted in crippling the investigation process to great extent.

15. Even though the husband of Smt.Madhuri has been arrested and during the pendency of the present petition, brother-in-law of the Smt. Madhuri being arrested, the police cannot come to a logical conclusion and file the appropriate report as is contemplated under Section 173 of the Cr.P.C for want of presence of the present petitioners.

16. Taking note of the age of the petitioners being 73 years and 67 years, directing the present petitioners to join the investigation and to under go limited period of custodial interrogation would not only facilitate the investigation process but also protects the rights of the parties in a balanced manner.

17. Taking note of the fact that the death has occurred within the 7 years of the marriage,
prosecution does enjoy the presumption as is available under Section 113A and 113B of the Indian Evidence Act.
Demand of dowry was spelt out by Smt. Madhuri during her life time, in the complaint lodged by her.
18. Subsequently, the father of the Smt. Madhuri has also reiterated the demand of dowry.
These aspects are to be investigated in an effective manner and appropriate report is to be filed by the investigation officer.

19. Whether at all the petitioners are also responsible for the act said to have been committed by the accused No.1 who is their son or not cannot be decided by this court at this stage by holding a mini trial and the same may futile the case of the parties during the trial one way or the other.

21. The petitioners, if directed to join the investigation, the same would facilitate investigation process as well.

22. The apprehension expressed by the prosecution could be met with by imposing suitable and stringent conditions including the petitioners to join the investigation and undergo custodial investigation for a limited period.

23. Accordingly, without expressing further opinion on the merits of the case, the following order is passed:
ORDER Petition against petitioner No.3 is dismissed in view of memo filed today reporting his arrest.
Petition against petitioners No.1 and 2 is allowed as under:
1.
The Criminal Petition is allowed.
2. Petitioners are directed to appear before the Investigating Officer on 28.04.2023 at 10.00 am.

3. Petitioners shall be taken to custody by the Investigating Officer and conclude the investigation process on the same day before 6.00 p.m. and thereafter enlarge the petitioners on bail by taking a bond for a sum of Rs.1,00,000/- (Rupees One Lakh only) each with one surety for the likesum to the satisfaction of the trial Court.
- 10 - 4.

The petitioners shall co-operate with the investigation agency and in that regard they shall mark their attendance on every third Sunday between 10.00 a.m. to 2.00 p.m. till the final report is filed.

5. Petitioners shall not tamper the prosecution witnesses evidence or hamper the investigation process in any manner and shall co-operate with the investigation process.
6.
Petitioners shall attend the Court regularly.
7. Petitioners shall not leave the jurisdiction of the Bangalore District without prior permission.
Violation of any one of the conditions would entitle the prosecution to seek for cancellation of the bail.
Ordered accordingly.
